qa_pairs.question: What is the ratio of the number of Asian immigrants arriving in the U.S. in 2022 to the sum of the number of Mexican - born and Indian - born immigrants in 2022, and then multiplied by the proportion of unauthorized immigrants in the U.S. foreign - born population in 2022?
qa_pairs.rationale: The proportion of Asian immigrants arriving in the U.S. in 2022 is 29% (chart_5-23). The number of Mexican - born immigrants in 2022 is 10.6 million (chart_3-1), and the number of Indian - born immigrants in 2022 is 2.8 million (chart_3-3). The proportion of unauthorized immigrants in the U.S. foreign - born population in 2022 is 23% (chart_6-1). First, find the sum of Mexican - born and Indian - born immigrants: 10.6 + 2.8 = 13.4 million. Then, assume the total number of immigrants arriving in 2022 is \(x\), the number of Asian immigrants arriving in 2022 is \(0.29x\). The ratio of the number of Asian immigrants arriving in 2022 to the sum of Mexican - born and Indian - born immigrants is \(\frac{0.29x}{13.4}\). Now multiply this ratio by the proportion of unauthorized immigrants (0.23): \(\frac{0.29x}{13.4}\times0.23\). If we assume \(x = 1\) (since the ratio is independent of the actual value of \(x\) in this case), the result is \(\frac{0.29\times0.23}{13.4}=\frac{0.0667}{13.4}\approx0.005 = 0.5\%.
